1:3.headline: Jonah runs from before God, not from God
1:3.body: The verse says Jonah fled מלפני, 'from before' God, not מפני, 'from' God. Radak and Malbim say no one can flee God himself. Jonah fled the land where prophecy comes, so God's word would not reach him.

sources.quote: אלא אין מלפני כמו מפני
sources.says: Radak says 'from before' is not the same as 'from'.

sources.quote: כי חשב שאם יצא מארץ ישראל לחוצה לארץ לא תשרה עליו רוח נבואה
sources.says: Radak says Jonah thought that once he left the Land of Israel, the spirit of prophecy would not rest on him.

sources.quote: שיש הבדל בין מפני ה' ובין מלפני ה'
sources.says: Malbim, citing Abarbanel, says there is a difference between 'from God' and 'from before God'.

sources.quote: מִן קֳדָם דְאִתְנַבֵּי בִּשְׁמָא דַייָ
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'from where he had prophesied in the name of the Lord'.

1:3.headline: A ship arriving from Tarshish, or about to sail there?
1:3.body: באה usually means 'coming'. Radak says the stress on the last syllable shows the ship was ready to sail to Tarshish. Malbim reads it as a ship that had just come back from Tarshish.

sources.quote: באה טעמו מלרע רוצה לומר שהיתה מוכנת ללכת ולבא תרשישה
sources.says: Radak says the word is stressed on the last syllable and means the ship was ready to go to Tarshish.

sources.quote: רק שהאניה באה עתה מתרשיש
sources.says: Malbim says the ship had just now come from Tarshish.

1:3.headline: Did Jonah pay his own fare, or hire the whole ship?
1:3.body: שכרה can mean 'her fare', the ship's whole hire. Rashi brings the midrash that Jonah paid for the entire ship. Ibn Ezra says he paid only his own share.

sources.quote: וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁנָּתַן שְׂכַר כֻּלָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says not only did he pay early, he paid the fare of the whole ship.

sources.quote: לא כל שכרה רק מה שהוא חייב ליתן בחלקו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it was not the whole fare, only what he owed for his part.

1:4.headline: The ship 'thought' it would break apart
1:4.body: The verse says the ship itself 'thought' it would break. Radak says this is a figure of speech: the people on board thought so. Ibn Ezra compares 'a land that sins against Me', where a land is spoken of as a person.

sources.quote: על דרך הרחבת הלשון, רוצה לומר אנשי האניה חשבו שתשבר האניה
sources.says: Radak says it is a figure of speech: the people on the ship thought it would break.

sources.quote: והאניה חשבה - כמו: ארץ כי תחטא לי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra compares it to 'a land that sins against Me'.

sources.quote: נִדְמֵית כְּאִלּוּ הִיא נִשְׁבֶּרֶת
sources.says: Rashi says it looked as if it were breaking.

1:6.headline: The captain is the chief of the rope-men
1:6.body: Radak and Ibn Ezra say sailors are called חובלים because they pull and loosen the ropes, חבלים, of the mast. Ibn Ezra also cites Rabbi Moshe, who reads it from תחבולות, clever plans.

sources.quote: כי הספנים נקראים חובלים לפי שמושכין ומתירין חבלי התורן
sources.says: Radak says sailors are called chovlim because they pull and loosen the ropes of the mast.

sources.quote: ורבי משה אמר: מגזרת תחבולות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites Rabbi Moshe that the word comes from tachbulot, strategies.

1:9.headline: Ivri: the people from across the river
1:9.body: Metzudat Zion says Israelites are called עברי because their roots are from עבר הנהר, across the river. Ibn Ezra says it means a child of Ever, who keeps the faith of that first Ever.

sources.quote: על כי מקור מחצבם מעבר הנהר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they are called this because their origin is from across the river.

sources.quote: שהוא מבני עבר הנקראים שהם על אמונת עבר הראשון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Jonah is of the children of Ever, who hold the faith of the first Ever.

1:9.headline: 'I fear the Lord': reverence, or fear of punishment?
1:9.body: Jonah says he fears the Lord. Radak reads it as reverence: he is a God-fearing man, not a cheat. Malbim cites Abarbanel, who reads it as fear: Jonah is afraid of being punished for running away.

sources.quote: כי אין מלאכתו מלאכת מרמה אבל הוא ירא את ה' ולא עושה כל עול
sources.says: Radak says his work is not deceit; he fears God and does no wrong.

sources.quote: שאני ירא מענשו על שברחתי מלפניו
sources.says: Malbim cites Abarbanel that Jonah means he fears God's punishment for fleeing from before Him.

1:10.headline: The sailors' great fear answers Jonah's 'I fear'
1:10.body: Jonah has just said 'I fear the Lord'. Ibn Ezra says the sailors' fear answers that word. Malbim says their first fear was of the storm, while this one is the fear of God.

sources.quote: וייראו - כנגד שאמר אני ירא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they feared in response to his saying 'I fear'.

sources.quote: היתה יראת הסכנה. אבל יראה זו היתה יראת ה'
sources.says: Malbim says the first fear was fear of danger, but this fear was fear of God.

1:13.headline: The sailors 'dig' through the sea with their oars
1:13.body: חתר means to dig through, as a thief digs through a wall. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say rowing hard against the waves looked like digging in the sea.

sources.quote: יָגְעוּ וְעָסְקוּ כְּחוֹתֵר בַּמַּחְתֶּרֶת
sources.says: Rashi says they toiled like one digging through a tunnel.

sources.quote: השיטו במשוטו׳ בתוך הים ונדמה כאלו חופרים בים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they rowed with oars in the sea, and it looked as if they were digging in the sea.

sources.quote: בעבור שבעלי המשוטות דומים לחותרים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is used because rowers look like diggers.

1:14.headline: Dying because of this man, or for killing him?
1:14.body: The sailors pray not to perish בנפש האיש הזה. Rashi reads it as 'for the sin of taking his life'. Malbim reads it the other way: if we keep him, we all drown because of his sin.

sources.quote: בֶּעָוֹן שֶׁנִּשְׁלַח יָד בְּנַפְשׁוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means for the sin of laying a hand on his life.

sources.quote: אם לא נשליכהו אל הים הלא נאבד אנחנו ע"י נפש האיש הזה
sources.says: Malbim says if we do not throw him into the sea, we will perish because of this man.

sources.quote: בנפש - בעבור כמו: ויעבד יעקב ברחל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the ב means 'for the sake of', as in 'Jacob served for Rachel'.

1:16.headline: How could they offer a sacrifice on a ship?
1:16.body: Radak asks how sailors could slaughter an offering at sea. He follows the Targum: they promised to bring an offering to God. Metzudat David says they took it on themselves to sacrifice at the Temple.

sources.quote: איך זבחו זבח בספינה אלא פירושו כתרגומו
sources.says: Radak asks how they could sacrifice on the ship, and says it should be read as the Targum does.

sources.quote: וַאֲמַרוּ לְדַבָּחָא דְבַח קֳדָם יְיָ
sources.says: The Targum says they promised to offer a sacrifice before the Lord.

sources.quote: קבלו על עצמם לזבוח לה׳ בבה״מ
sources.says: Metzudat David says they took it upon themselves to sacrifice to God in the Temple.

4:4.headline: 'Are you very angry?' or 'Does My goodness anger you?'
4:4.body: Radak reads ההיטב as 'very', so God asks if Jonah is deeply angry. Radak also cites others who read it 'does the good I do them anger you?', a view Ibn Ezra calls empty.

sources.quote: והיטב ענינו חוזק הענין
sources.says: Radak says היטב means strength or intensity, and also brings a reading 'does the good I do them anger you'.

sources.quote: ויש מפרשים אם הטוב שאני עושה להם חרה לך
sources.says: Radak cites some who explain it as 'are you angry at the good I do for them'.

sources.quote: ויפת אמר: היחר לך שאיטב אני למי שארצה. וזה הבל הוא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that Yefet read it 'are you angry that I do good to whom I choose', and calls that nonsense.

4:6.headline: Saved from 'his evil', meaning the burning sun
4:6.body: רעה usually means evil or harm. Rashi says here it is the sun's heat, and Ibn Ezra brings a view that Jonah's skin had gone soft from his long stay inside the fish.

sources.quote: לְהַצִּיל לוֹ מֵרָעָתוֹ. מֵחוֹם הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says 'his evil' means the heat of the sun.

sources.quote: כי בעבור שעמד במעי הדג זמן ארוך, עור בשרו רך ולא יוכל לסבול החום
sources.says: Ibn Ezra brings a view that after his long time in the fish his skin was soft and could not bear the heat.
